A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIRCSE study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GIRCSE evaluations, component ablations and scaling analyses, including MTEB, instruction-following, NanoBEIR and TREC results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports training-loss and gradient-norm trajectories in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Soft-token generation, generated-state pooling, stepwise contrastive supervision and refinement regularization are unchanged. The pseudocode added to the main text repeats v1's Appendix D algorithm; correcting 'Transformer encoder' to 'Transformer decoder' does not change the architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data and evaluate English MTEB, IntentEmotion, NYTClustering, NanoBEIR and TREC tasks. The added training diagnostics concern the existing Mistral-7B/200K configuration and introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2, 3, 8 and 9 and Figures 2–3, including the Causal-EOS and Bidirectional-Avg baselines and two-stage generative variants. The new training diagnostics introduce no additional comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds a diagnostic evaluation tracking training loss and gradient L2 norm against global step for GIRCSE-Mistral7B-200K. Existing benchmark metrics, training budgets, hyperparameters and generation-length settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix G examines possible instability from soft-token training through loss and gradient-norm curves (Figures 4–5). Existing component ablations, generation-length analyses, token examples and model/data-scale comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 4–5 newly report EMA-smoothed summaries alongside raw training traces, and Figure 5 discloses removal of the top 2% of gradient outliers. This adds limited statistical processing information; repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals and the existing significance-reporting convention are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds loss and gradient-norm trajectories showing substantial early declines followed by low values in the illustrated training configuration. Existing benchmark, ablation and efficiency results are unchanged; for example, Table 2 retains GIRCSE MTEB averages of 67.83 and 67.67.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the computational and memory derivations in Equations 9–10 are unchanged. The latter move from v1 Appendix F to v2 Appendix E. The added stability discussion supplies empirical evidence, without a new formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: generative embedding refinement, competitive general-purpose and instruction-following performance, and improved embeddings with additional inference steps.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly raises gradient instability as a concern and interprets the added training curves as evidence of stable convergence. Existing interpretations of semantic refinement, test-time scaling, data efficiency and computational overhead remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a project repository link and states that code and pretrained models are available. v1 supplied comparator checkpoint links but lacked this project access pointer. Hyperparameters, baseline implementation descriptions and dataset instructions are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged, including the positioning relative to conventional LLM embeddings and Inbedder. No cited work or substantive novelty comparison is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited terminology corrections, adds a training-summary paragraph and acknowledgments, updates affiliations, and reorganizes several appendix headings. Most prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 4–5 and displays the existing pseudocode in the main text as Algorithm 1 while retaining a duplicate as Algorithm 2 in the appendix. Existing figures and tables retain their designs and contents, with changed placement and added conference headers.

improvement.justification: The new training diagnostics and explicit code/model access pointer modestly improve transparency. The gain is limited: benchmark evidence is unchanged, the gradient plot excludes the top 2% of outliers, and the new training-summary paragraph points to duplicated generation pseudocode rather than a training algorithm. These shortcomings constrain the benefit without outweighing the useful additions.
